turns.replyText:
Can you explain the main options in simple terms?
The main options come down to the season you need pollination for:
• Spring Mason Bees: Active in early spring (above 55°F) for spring blooms and fruit trees. They use moist, clay-rich mud to build their nests.
• Summer Leafcutter Bees: Active in summer (above 75°F) for summer vegetables and flowers. They use pieces of cut leaves to build their nests.
• Dual-Season Kits: Include nesting materials and cocoons for both Spring Mason bees and Summer Leafcutter bees, covering your entire growing season in one setup.
Starter Kits With Mason And Leafcutter Bees

turns.q: Is there anything else a beginner needs to get started?
turns.replyTail:
beginners just need a few basic yard conditions:
menu
• Location: Mount your bee house 3 to 6 feet off the ground on a sturdy wall or fence facing morning sun (east to southeast) with protection from wind and rain.
• Flowers & Water: Have nectar- and pollen-rich flowers within ~300 feet, and a shallow water dish with landing stones.
• Mud (for Mason Bees): Moist, clay-rich mud within 10 to 20 feet of the house so they can seal their nesting chambers.
